label: text
text: (To the Editor of the China Mail).

label: text
text: Sir,—All these rent amendments in the Hongkong Revised Rent Ordinance for the ensuing year do not help the tenants but in a very small way. What the tenants in Hongkong require is a Tenants Union and a few rules like the following may be put in force:—

label: text
text: (1) To pay the landlords the rents according to the valuation of the houses and properties, and no more and also to make such valuation as a standard "rental" for all time and for all tenants both new and old alike.

label: text
text: (2) To refuse to shift from the house occupied for either the landlord's friends or his wealthy clients from Canton or elsewhere.

label: text
text: (4) The landlords to be made when called upon to effect any necessary repairs and make good same. If the landlord refuses to do so the tenants to do the repairs and deduct same from the rents.

label: text
text: (3) To pay the landlord's rentals for what the house is worth and no more.

label: text
text: (5) Tenants may be made not to occupy any houses without a permit from the Tenants Union. If contrary a penalty of $500.00 for the offence be inflicted on such tenants that disobey this order.

label: text
text: Some of the enterprising European and Chinese gentlemen in Hongkong should start a canvassing campaign for the creation of the Tenants Union. They will find that they will have all and every body in Hongkong joining in it. A small sum of 50 cents as an entrance fee and 50 cents as a yearly subscription every man, woman, girl, boy and child will become a member of the Union.

label: text
text: (6) The amount of house rents to be valued by "The Tenants Union and by a local Architect, Many more rules to be made to meet the tenants" and the landlords both way.

label: text
text: There are many more and other Unions allowed in Hongkong, so why can't the Hongkong tenants have a Union of their own? Surely there is no harm. Let'the people of Hongkong look after themselves and not let the grasping landiords do what they like and think fit.

label: text
text: (To the Editor of the China Mail.)

label: text
text: Sir. "This Isle of Fragrant Streams is what it is notorious for, just because of people like 'Not Jealous' who will place the meanest constructions possible on anything not entirely in accord with their creed. Reading my letter as a whole you will, Sir, I feel, disagree that 'I have an axe to grind,' that it was'such an unfair attack,' and that 'it serves no good purpose except to arouse racial antagonisms' — as. "Not Jealous" suggests.

label: text
text: If the Americans came here to play the Chinese—although I refuse to believe what your correspondent makes out—do Honda, O'Callaghan and Tottenham represent the Chinese?

label: text
text: By your being so good as to publish my letter, readers gather the impression that you are of the opinion it does serve some good purpose even if "Not Jealous" says "No."

label: text
text: My grouse is that Honda is only asked to play one match to three each by O'Callughan and Ng Szewong, and two by Tottenham. Admitted that Honda is only a better-than-moderate doubles player, he deserves, as champion of the Colony and former champion of the F.M.S. and in view of Kinsey's praise for Japanese tennis prowess, to get a showing in at least one of the doubles matches.

label: text
text:
It was while on the subject of the selection that I made—at least, I conscientiously intended—a casual reference to the Rumahna's being passed over. "Not jealous" flares up and accuses me of insinuations which were as far from me as any slight on Ng Szewong whom I will go one further by pointing to as the model of sportsmanship, although I cannot help feeling he has been a little lethargic. He disappointed many admirers and me by standing out of the tournament whatever his reasons may have been. Petty is the only description I can label on to an unwarranted, nasty, unsportsmanlike criticism my supposed nationality, based misunderstanding and narrow-mindedness and made in carping grit.
Yours, etc.,
[Further allusions to nationality will be excised from our correspondents' letters. "Reformer" is quite wrong when he infers that the Editor shares his views by publishing the letter. The Editor accepts no responsibility for the views of his correspondents and his attitude, unless defined in the editorial columns, is strictly neutral. — Editor, "China Mail."]

Another Bathing
Scandal

label: text
text: Sir.—As it would appear that your correspondents who drew attention to a nuisance at Repulse Bay beach were largely instrumental in getting the matter put right. I venture to write in the note that my comments in regard to another matter there may also be brought to the attention of the proper authorities and something be put in hand.

label: text
text: (To the Editor of the China Mail.)

label: text
text: The beach is in a terrible state at present with piled up boulders near the sea-front and sharp stones strewn for some way out. The only spot where it is possible to enter the water with any degree of comfort is by the tents but it is surely too much to expect bathers to walk a hundred yards or more as they have to in some cases.

label: text
text: which has resulted in the marrying of the Colony's most popular Leuch I cannot explain, but much of it is probably due to the last tephoon and if the stones were once got rid of I do not think that there would be much likelihood of any more returning.

label: text
text: The bather who is a poor or non-swimmer is in a bad way, for instead of being able to venture in so far as he likes and out when he likes it is a question of having to go in entirely and out only when one has finished for good.

label: text
text: In the event of the authorities not feeling disposed to move in the matter what about the owners of mat-sheds inaugurating a fund to which each could contribute, say, a dollar, by which coolie hire for the removal of the stones could be paid?

label: paragraph_title
text: Boxing.

label: text
text: [To the Editor of the China Mail.]

label: text
text: Sir,—I have just been reading the opinion of an Australian sportsman, who says there should be no purses in boxing, but that each man should be paid a percentage on his drawing power. The Stadium at Sydney retains 5¢ per cent. of the takings and the fighters split the other 50. He suggests a better scheme in a winner's and loser's end; say 60 and 40 per cent. Perhaps Hong Kong is too small a place to adopt such an idea; but one cannot get away from the idea that where a man is likely to receive a large sum, win, lose or draw, the fighting is not likely to be so good as, presumably, it would be; if his winnings depended on whether he won or lost.

label: paragraph_title
text: ANOTHER OPERA?

label: paragraph_title
text: PHILHARMONIC SOCIETY ACTIVITIES.

label: text
text: COMMITTEE TO DECIDE

label: text
text: It is probable that Hongkong will have another light opera this winter if the feeling of those attending a special meeting of the Philharmonic Society held at the Cathedral Hall yesterday afternoon is at all representative. The meeting considered the replies received to the questionnaire circulated to members.

label: text
text: Mr. S. Collett took the chair in the absence of Sir Claud Severn and after explaining that the policy of the Society was indefinite in many respects he called upon Mr. Mills, the Hon. Secretary, to address the meeting on the subject of the replies received to the questionnaire.

label: text
text: Mr. Mills said that 45 replies had been received out of 120 forms circulated. Twenty-eight specified a preference for light.opera alone, 13 were for one opera and one concert and four for the confining of the society's activities to concerts only. Although preference had been so indicated, 34 of those who replied were ready to participate in whatever policy was adopted and 11 failed to express an opinion on the point.

label: text
text: The Chairman then tabled a proposal by Mr. Mills and seconded by Mr. G. H. Piercy, that the meeting was in favour of the production of one light opera and at least one concert during the forthcoming season.

label: text
text: This was eventually carried unanimously, although Mr. Gillingham expressed the opinion that as Mr. W. G. Wheeler was leaving the Colony the question of a producer should be decided first.

label: text
text: The meeting was thrown open for a short time for the purpose of receiving suggestions as to a suitable opera to produce, those receiving most support being Iolanthe and Merrie England, Pirates of Penzance had many supporters but it was thought that this was outside the scope of the Society. Les Cloches de Corneville was suggested by a member but received no support, nor did the Maid of the Mountains, one of the suggestions sent in. Other suggestions sent in were for the production of Cyrano de Bergerac, Rebel Maid, Highwayman Love and Veronique.

label: text
text: On the proposition of Mr. Penny, seconded by Mr. Gillingham, the matter of the choice of an opera was left to be decided by the Committee.

label: text
text: Election of officers followed, Miss Mow Fung being appointed to the post of treasurer and Mr. Gillingham, Honorary Secretary with Mr. Jefford as Assistant.

label: paragraph_title
text: TRAVELLER'S PERSONAL

label: text
text: DEBATE IN HOUSE.

label: text
text: BROADENING THE BASIS OF

label: text
text: In the House of Commons, the Chancellor of the Exchequer, Mr. Winston Churchill, announced that the present scale of the silk duties was not in all details the absolute final.

label: paragraph_title
text: LONDON, May 11.

label: text
text: "Immediately the Budget resolutions had been finally passed, he would begin discussions with the real and artificial silk trades and associations."

label: text
text: The Government merely asked the House to assent to the principle of a silk tax, after which all parties, including the Government, would be free to revise the present scale.

label: text
text: Mr. Churchill said it was impossible to tax real silk and leave artificial silk free which would cripple and destroy the natural silk industry. Both must be treated equally. This was attempted in the proposed scale which, however, was subject to revision.

label: text
text: He announced regarding made, up importations that there would be a reasonable personal allowance for travellers in order that no appreciable inconvenience might be suffered by the travelling public.

label: text
text: Provisional agreement with the trade had been reached regarding made-up importations containing only a proportion of silk on a basis of a lower duty when the silk content did not exceed twenty per cent. and a possibly still lower duty for articles containing only the smallest proportion of silk.

label: text
text: Mr. Churchill in conclusion said he did not see why the tax on a raw material like silk should be considered monstrous when all the Governments for years past had taxed sugar.

label: text
text: The actual Reduced rate had not yet been fixed. Mr. Churchill said that silk taxes were an essential part of the Government's policy of broadening the basis of taxation.

label: text
text: Sir Alfred 'Mond (Labour), opposing the duties, said that when he was recently in the East he had been filled with alarm on going into the Bazaars in Syria and elsewhere to see British textile goods rapidly being replaced by goods from Japan, Czechoslovakia and Italy.

label: text
text: Labour amendments postponing the operation of the silk duties from July 1, to December 1, and omitting the customs duty on artificial silk were both rejected, and at the report stage of the Budget resolutions authorising the customs and excise duties on silk were carried by 330 to 166 votes, thereby completing the report stage of all the Budget resolutions, after which the Finance Bill founded thereupon was introduced by Mr. Churchill, and read for the first time.

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: In the House of Commons Ltd. Col. W. Guinness, Financial Secretary of the Treasury, replying to Mr. V. A. Cazalet (Conservative), said Poland's indebtedness to Britain consisted of a relief debt of £4,770,000 also of £167,585 for the repatriation of Polish prisoners from Siberia after the war.

label: text

label: text
text: The Soviet Government has decided to recall Voline following the French Government's protests against his speech.

label: text
text: Paris, April 29.—A Soviet embassy communique denies that it has in any way participated in Communist propaganda. The Matin, however, states that the Government has opened an enquiry in regard to a speech delivered by M. Voline, the first secretary, of the embassy, at a meeting organised by Chinese residents of Paris, after the death of Dr. Sun Yat-sen and a diplomatic sequel is certain. The embassy argues that the funeral oration cannot be regarded as an unfriendly act. Ambassador Krassin conversing with M. Briand, declared that he was not participating in subversive propaganda.

label: paragraph_title
text: DEATH OF SIX FIJI EUROPEANS.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text:
Six Europeans and four Indians have died from typhoid, but the chief medical officer holds the opinion that the outbreak is abating. Doctors are arriving this week from Sydney and Auckland.
[Earlier cables stated that a hundred Europeans and many Indians were suffering from typhoid. Extra doctors are being sent from Australia and New Zealand.]

label: text
text: Peking, May 11.—The student agitation appears to be quietening down—on a result of a medatory efforts on the part of government officials. A mandate was issued last night reproving the students for violent conduct and advising them to carry on with their studies, emphasizing that the government did not wish to gain a reputation for leniency by encouraging disorderly conduct in the trend of the educational movement.—Renter.

label: text
text: ALLEGED RECEIVING.

label: text
text: The remand cases in which ten persons were charged with receiving and with having unlawful possession of 146 bags of sugar, valued at $2,920, before Mr. S. B. B. McElderry at the Central Magistracy last Tuesday, were resumed this morning. The cargo was the property of Messrs. Jardine, Matheson & Co., Ltd.

label: text
text: In the first case a managing partner of the Wing Sing shop, of 173, Des Vœux Road West, was charged along with five other employees with receiving the cargo, similar charge being framed against another man who was alleged to have stored the sugar in a godown and later removed a part of the cargo. Detective Inspector T. Murphy informed His Worship that he was not producing any evidence against the seven persons, and they were discharged Mr. J. A. Leask appeared for the first defendant, Mr. M. K. Lo, for four of the other's in the same case, and Mr. C. A. S. Russ for the defendant in the other case.

label: text
text: The case against three boatwomen for unlawful possession of 46 bags of sugar, part of the stolen cargo, was adjourned until next week, Mr. E. S. C. Brooks appearing for the defence.

DISPUTED, WILL CASE
EVIDENCE.

label: text
text: The grandson of a Hawaiian phunter whose $1,000,000 will is engaging the attention of the Hongkong Court, stated in evidence this morning that his uncle shortly after the death of the grandfather told him that he benefited under the will but would be allowed only $500 a year for the present. Later, witness stated, when another brother of the deceased pressed for a full distribution of the property, the uncle told him (witness) that he benefited to the extent of $40,000 and paid him this in shares in the Hongkong and Shanghai Bank.

label: text
text: This witness is plaintiff in an action brought against the uncle mentioned who is a former Civil Governor of Canton. His name is Chan Wing-On, that of the uncle Chan Chik-ye, and of the deceased Chian Atong.

label: text
text:
The whole of this morning's proceedings were taken up with the evidence of the plaintiff, examined by Mr. Elsley Zeitlyn and cross-examined by Mr. F. C. Jenkin.
The early cross-examination was largely in the nature of an enquiry into the names of the plaintiff's wives and their status and His Lordship stopped it after some time on the grounds of irrelevance.

label: text
text: Mr. F. C. Jenkins together with Mr. T. Addis (both instructed by Mr. F. C. Hall) represented the defendant.

label: text
text: The Hon. Mr. C. G. Alabaster, K.C. (instructed by Mr. H. K. Woo) represents three sub-poenned executives, of a deceased brother of Chan Aiong.
